lexingCheck: Token streams are hand-derived (harness/vector_sources.py); check_vectors.py re-lexes every input with tslex.py and harness/crosscheck.js compares them with the TypeScript 6.0.3 parser and scanner.

vectors.description: Element with a string attribute, text and an expression container.
JSX text holding '//' and reserved words is one jsx-text token per run.
vectors.inputText:
const p =

vectors.description: Names inside a tag are ident, including 'class', 'for' and 'data-x'.
Fragments, member and namespaced names, JSX in a conditional.
'<' after an expression end is an operator or type-argument opener; after '&&' it opens JSX.
vectors.inputText: if (a < b && c > d) f(x); const e = ok && {a < b};

vectors.description: '<T,>' and '<T extends X>' are generic arrows, not JSX.
vectors.inputText:
const id = <T,>(x: T) => x;
const g = <T extends object>(x: T) => x;

vectors.description: '<const T,>' is a generic arrow.
'<T extends=' is JSX with an attribute named 'extends'.
White-space-only JSX text is trivia; other text is trimmed at both ends but keeps inner spaces.
An element directly after '=' is an attribute value.
An expression container starts in regex position.
Templates inside attribute and child containers.
Plain JavaScript lexes the same under tsx-tokens.
vectors.inputText:
var r = a / b / c, s = /=/g;
if (r) /x/.exec(s);

vectors.description: JSX layout pair, one line.
JSX layout pair, one attribute per line and indented text.
A comment-only container yields '{' '}'.
Known limitation: a generic function type after '=' opens JSX; '>' in JSX text is then illegal.
The ts-type-assertion input under tsx-tokens: '<T>' opens an element that never closes.
'>' is not allowed in JSX text.
'}' is not allowed in JSX text.
End of input inside an element.
A closing tag with no open element.
Unterminated JSX attribute string.
'<!--' in expression position opens JSX; '!' is illegal.
Only '>' may follow '/' in an opening tag.
After an element ends in normal mode, '/' is division.
JSX text is trimmed with the full trivia set, including U+00A0.
Trivia may separate '=' from an attribute-value element.
The name after 'const' is not checked against reserved words.
'extendsX' is not 'extends': the '<' is JSX.
'<' in a tag is allowed only right after '='.
An escape in a look-ahead name makes the '<' JSX; '\' is then illegal in the tag.
Unterminated comment after 'extends' in the look-ahead: JSX, then unterminated-comment in tag mode.
